{{Short description|Type of ordinary differential equation}}
In the study of [[diffusion flame]], '''Liñán's equation''' is a second-order nonlinear [[ordinary differential equation]] which describes the inner structure of the diffusion flame, first derived by [[Amable Liñán]] in 1974.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Linan |first=A. |year=1974 |title=The asymptotic structure of counterflow diffusion flames for large activation energies |journal=Acta Astronautica |volume=1 |issue=7–8 |pages=1007–1039 |doi=10.1016/0094-5765(74)90066-6 |bibcode=1974AcAau...1.1007L |url=https://oa.upm.es/927/ }}</ref> The equation reads as

:<math>\frac{d^2y}{d\zeta^2} =(y^2-\zeta^2)e^{-\delta^{-1/3}(y+\gamma \zeta)} </math>

subjected to the boundary conditions

:<math>
\begin{align}
\zeta\rightarrow -\infty : &\quad \frac{dy}{d\zeta}=-1,\\
\zeta\rightarrow +\infty : &\quad \frac{dy}{d\zeta}=+1
\end{align}</math>

where <math>\delta</math> is the reduced or rescaled [[Damköhler numbers|Damköhler number]] and <math>\gamma</math> is the ratio of excess heat conducted to one side of the reaction sheet to the total heat generated in the reaction zone. If <math>\gamma>0</math>, more heat is transported to the oxidizer side, thereby reducing the [[reaction rate]] on the oxidizer side (since reaction rate depends on the temperature) and consequently greater amount of fuel will be leaked into the oxidizer side. Whereas, if <math>\gamma<0</math>, more heat is transported to the fuel side of the diffusion flame, thereby reducing the reaction rate on the fuel side of the flame and increasing the oxidizer leakage into the fuel side. When <math>\gamma\rightarrow 1</math> <math>(\gamma\rightarrow -1)</math>, all the heat is transported to the oxidizer (fuel) side  and therefore the flame sustains extremely large amount of fuel (oxidizer) leakage.<ref>Gubernov, V., & Kim, J. S. (2006). On the fast-time oscillatory instabilities of Linan's diffusion-flame regime. Combustion Theory and Modelling, 10(5), 749-770.</ref>

The equation is, in some aspects, universal (also called the canonical equation of the diffusion flame) since although Liñán derived the equation for [[stagnation point flow]], assuming unity [[Lewis number|Lewis numbers]] for the reactants, the same equation is found to represent the inner structure for general laminar flamelets,<ref>Peters, N., & Williams, F. A. (1983). Liftoff characteristics of turbulent jet diffusion flames. AIAA journal, 21(3), 423-429.</ref><ref>Peters, N. (1983). Local quenching due to flame stretch and non-premixed turbulent combustion. Combustion Science and Technology, 30(1–6), 1–17.</ref><ref>Peters, N. (1986). Laminar Flamelet concept in turbulent combustion Twenty-First Symposium (International) on Combustion-The Combustion Institute 1231.</ref> having arbitrary Lewis numbers.<ref>Seshadri, K., & Trevino, C. (1989). The influence of the Lewis numbers of the reactants on the asymptotic structure of counterflow and stagnant diffusion flames. Combustion science and technology, 64(4-6), 243-261.</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cheatham |first1=S. |last2=Matalon |first2=M. |year=2000 |title=A general asymptotic theory of diffusion flames with application to cellular instability |journal=Journal of Fluid Mechanics |volume=414 |issue=1 |pages=105–144 |doi=10.1017/S0022112000008752 |bibcode=2000JFM...414..105C |s2cid=121996206 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Liñán |first1=A. |last2=Martínez-Ruiz |first2=D. |last3=Vera |first3=M. |last4=Sánchez |first4=A. L. |year=2017 |title=The large-activation-energy analysis of extinction of counterflow diffusion flames with non-unity Lewis numbers of the fuel |journal=Combustion and Flame |volume=175 |pages=91–106 |doi=10.1016/j.combustflame.2016.06.030 |bibcode=2017CoFl..175...91L |url=https://oa.upm.es/50877/ }}</ref>

An alterernate equation, known as '''Liñán's equation for the premixed-flame regime''' is given by<ref>Lee, S. R., & Kim, J. S. (2024). Linear Stability of the Activation-Energy-Asymptotics Reactive-Layer Structure: I. Liñán’s Premixed-Flame Regime. Combustion Science and Technology, 196(16), 4242-4268.</ref>

:<math>\frac{d^2f}{d\zeta^2} =\Lambda f e^{-(f+m\zeta)} </math>

subjected to the boundary conditions

:<math>
\begin{align}
\zeta\rightarrow -\infty : &\quad \frac{df}{d\zeta}=-1,\\
\zeta\rightarrow +\infty : &\quad \frac{df}{d\zeta}=0.
\end{align}</math>

==Existence of solutions==

Near the extinction of the diffusion flame, <math>\delta</math> is order unity. The equation has no solution for <math>\delta<\delta_E</math>, where <math>\delta_E</math> is the extinction Damköhler number. For <math>\delta>\delta_E</math> with <math>|\gamma|<1</math>, the equation possess two solutions, of which one is an unstable solution. Unique solution exist if <math>|\gamma|>1</math> and <math>\delta>\delta_E</math>. The solution is unique for <math>\delta>\delta_I</math>, where <math>\delta_I</math> is the ignition Damköhler number.

Liñán also gave a correlation formula for the extinction Damköhler number, which is increasingly accurate for <math>1-\gamma \ll 1</math>,

:<math>\delta_E = e[(1-\gamma)-(1-\gamma)^2+0.26(1-\gamma)^3 + 0.055(1-\gamma)^4].</math>

==Generalized Liñán's equation==
The generalized Liñán's equation is given by

:<math>\frac{d^2y}{d\zeta^2} =(y-\zeta)^m (y+\zeta)^ne^{-\delta^{-1/3}(y+\gamma \zeta)} </math>

where <math>m</math> and <math>n</math> are constant reaction orders of fuel and oxidizer, respectively.

==Large Damköhler number limit==
In the [[Burke–Schumann limit]], <math>\delta\rightarrow\infty</math>. Then the equation reduces to

:<math>\frac{d^2y}{d\zeta^2} = (y-\zeta)^m(y+\zeta)^n, \quad \zeta\rightarrow\pm\infty:\, \frac{dy}{d\zeta}=\pm 1. </math>

An approximate solution to this equation was developed by Liñán himself using integral method in 1963 for his thesis,<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Liñán |first=A. |year=1963 |title=On the Structure of Laminar Diffusion Flames |publisher=[[California Institute of Technology]] |type=Ph.D. thesis |url=https://resolver.caltech.edu/CaltechETD:etd-12072005-134536 }}</ref>

:<math>y(\zeta)=y_m + (\zeta-\zeta_m)\operatorname{erf}[k (\zeta-\zeta_m)] - \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi} k}\left[1-e^{-k^2 (\zeta-\zeta_m)^2}\right],</math>

where <math>\mathrm{erf}</math> is the [[error function]] and 

:<math>\begin{align}
\zeta_m &= \frac{n-m}{n+m} y_m,\\
y_m &= \frac{m+n}{2}\left[\frac{2}{\pi m^2n^2}\left(\sqrt{1+\frac{\pi(m+n)}{2mn}}-1\right)\right]^{\frac{1}{m+n+1}},\\
k &= \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} m^m n^n\left(\frac{2y_m}{m+n}\right)^{m+n}.
\end{align}
</math>
Here <math>\zeta=\zeta_m</math> is the location where <math>y(\zeta)</math> reaches its minimum value <math>y(\zeta_m)=y_m</math>. When <math>m=n=1</math>, <math>\zeta_m=0</math>, <math>y_m=0.8702</math> and <math>k=0.6711</math>.
